# Architecture decisions
Compact ADRs. Status values: Proposed (needs spike evidence), Accepted, Superseded. Evidence lines are appended with dates by spikes and reviews (`Evidence YYYY-MM-DD:`). Date of initial decisions: 2026-09-26.

## ADR-001 UI stack
Status: Accepted
Context: Native Android, one tablet, modern animated UI, lowest pen latency.
Options: A Kotlin + Jetpack Compose UI with a View-based canvas host; B Compose-only canvas; C Flutter / cross-platform.
Decision: A. Compose for all chrome (library, toolbar, sheets, settings). The canvas is a custom `CanvasHostView` embedded with `AndroidView`, with androidx.ink's `InProgressStrokesView` on top.
Consequences: pen input bypasses recomposition; Compose remains the productive default elsewhere. Two UI toolkits meet at one well-defined seam (`CanvasController`).

## ADR-002 Ink stack
Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S1)
Context: Wet ink must be as low-latency as possible (R-INK-08); strokes need pressure/tilt brushes, geometry for erasing and lasso, and stable rendering.
Options: A androidx.ink 1.1.0-alpha (newest alpha; public brush customization API, fixes since 1.0.0); B androidx.ink 1.0.0 stable (Dec 2025); C custom renderer on androidx.graphics front-buffered surfaces.
Decision: A, pinned to an exact alpha. Front-buffered wet ink via `InProgressStrokesView`, finished strokes via `CanvasStrokeRenderer`, geometry for erase/lasso. The experimental mesh-editing partial eraser (1.1.0-alpha05+) is not used because its results are not yet serializable; Folio splits stroke inputs instead (06-ink-input.md#erasers). Our file format stores our own `StrokeInputs`, not ink's serialization, so a library change never breaks files.
Fallback: B if an alpha regresses on the device; C only if the spike proves ink unusable on HyperOS.
Revisit: when ink 1.1.0 goes stable (move to stable).
Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S1): Pad 7, debug build, ink 1.1.0-alpha09, route `spike-ink` (pressure pen, CanvasStrokeRenderer page, DisplayModeHelper), 50 synthetic `input stylus swipe` strokes per run (400 ms, 50 events each). Median of runs, worst in brackets.
| Handoff mode | Runs | `ink:onTouch` p50 / p95 / max ms | `ink:handoff` p50 / p95 ms | Janky frames | 3 screenshots after pen-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| commit (ViewTreeObserver frame-commit callback) | 3 | 0.20 / 0.28 (0.29) / 0.55 (0.63) | 6.4 / 8.8 (one 66 ms outlier) | 0.8% (1.6%) | stroke shown, all 3 |
| frame (Choreographer frame callback) | 1 | 0.20 / 0.28 / 0.49 | 7.8 / 8.2 | 0.4% | stroke shown, all 3 |
| immediate (inside `onStrokesFinished`) | 1 | 0.20 / 0.27 / 0.66 | 0.03 / 0.05 | 0.7% | stroke shown, all 3 |
Front buffer works on HyperOS: InProgressStrokesView adds a SurfaceView (BLAST, z=1) above the window on the first stroke. Requesting the 144 Hz mode left the display at 120 Hz (device.md#display). Screenshots settle >= 100 ms after pen-up, so single-frame flicker and felt latency are a USER-CHECK. Motion prediction was not wired in the spike (P03).
Decision 2026-09-27: A confirmed (p95 0.29 ms vs 1 ms budget, handoff clean). Handoff mode: commit, the only mode that removes wet strokes after the frame showing the committed stroke by construction (A-005).

## ADR-003 Committed content rendering
Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S2)
Context: Dense pages (1500+ strokes, text, images) must pan/zoom at 144 Hz.
Options: A software bitmap tiles (512 px) rendered off the main thread; B RenderNode tiles with compositing layers (GPU-cached display lists); C draw all objects every frame.
Decision (default): A, because the same code path serves PNG export and it is portable; B if it wins the spike clearly on jank. C rejected (cost grows with content).
Consequences: memory budget and tile invalidation logic required; zoom shows scaled tiles briefly until the new bucket renders.
Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S2b): Pad 7, route `spike-tiles`, A4 lined page, 1500 seeded strokes (pen/marker/highlighter), 512 px tiles, CanvasStrokeRenderer on a software canvas (A) or RenderNode recording with a compositing layer (B); 3 runs per strategy, median (worst). Display ran at 120 Hz (144 requested). Zoom 1 = bucket 5 (42 tiles incl. ring), zoom 3 = bucket 8.
| Metric | A bitmap tiles | B RenderNode tiles |
|---|---|---|
| zoom-anim 1->3->1 (800 ms each) janky % / p95 / p99 ms | 0.49 (0.50) / 15 (18) / 24 (28) | 0.49 (0.49) / 18 (18) / 22 (24) |
| 10 s finger pan at zoom 3, janky % / p95 / p99 ms | 0.06 (0.06) / 9 (9) / 10 (11) | 0.06 (0.06) / 9 (9) / 10 (11) |
| tile render p50 / p95 ms, bucket 5 | 3.72 / 8.02 (17.3) | 3.63 / 8.38 (9.29) (recording only; raster happens on the RenderThread) |
| tile render p50 / p95 ms, bucket 8 | 2.24 / 4.35 (5.19) | 1.96 / 4.00 (4.22) |
| settle (all visible tiles of a new bucket) p50 ms | 97 (106) | 80 (94) |
| `tiles:draw` p95 ms | 1.11 (1.39) | 0.82 (1.09) |
| meminfo PSS / Graphics / Native heap MiB | 426 / 148 / 202 (Native drops to 125 within seconds) | 272 / 126 / 71 |
| pixels differing from a direct software render (zoom 1 / 3) | 0.001% / 0.002% | 1.16% / 0.41% (GPU antialiasing differs) |
Both strategies stay far below 1% janky frames and are tied on jank; screenshots show no seams or missing tiles.
Decision 2026-09-27: A (tie rule; also pixel-identical to the export raster path). B's lower memory is noted; the tile cache budget (05-canvas-rendering.md#tiles, 25% of largeMemoryClass) must bound A's bitmaps (P03).

## ADR-004 Library storage
Status: Accepted (2026-09-28, P01-S6)
Context: User-visible folder for cross-platform copying (R-FILE-01); fast scanning and random-access ZIP reads; personal sideloaded app.
Options: A `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` + `java.io.File` in `Documents/Folio`; B Storage Access Framework tree URI + DocumentFile; C app-specific external storage (`Android/data`), hidden from most file managers.
Decision: A. Debug builds use `Documents/Folio-Debug` so tests never touch real notes.
Consequences: one-time permission screen; not Play-Store compatible (irrelevant for sideloading). B stays the migration path if a future Android version restricts A.
Evidence 2026-09-28 (P01-S6): Pad 7, route `spike-io`, All-files access granted, java.io on `/sdcard/Documents/Folio-Debug` (FUSE). Working copy in app files: 4 x 10 MB random assets (STORED) + 10 x 1 MB pages (DEFLATED) -> 46.0 MB `.folio`.
| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Pack (CRC + ZIP write + fsync + rename + directory fsync), 4 runs | 1391 / 1410 / 1413 / 1450 ms (write 1282..1363, fsync 35..39, rename 13..57, CRC 33..40); directory fsync supported |
| Read-back verify (all entries, CRC checked) | ok, 16 entries, mimetype first |
| App killed (`stop.sh`) mid-pack, 3 runs | target intact and valid every time; tmp removed by start-up cleanup (1 run) or already gone after the kill (2 runs, FUSE dropped the half-written file) |
| FileObserver on `Folio-Debug/fixtures` for `push-fixture.sh` (external writer through FUSE) | CREATE + CLOSE_WRITE (DELETE first when replacing) delivered, under about 150 ms after the push (bound limited by the 6 s `debugcmd.sh` round trip) |
| FileObserver during our own pack | CREATE `.tmp`, CLOSE_WRITE, MOVED_FROM `.tmp`, MOVED_TO target |
Decision 2026-09-28: A confirmed. Pack stays within 1.5 s for 46 MB with little margin (P11 budget watch: most time is the FUSE write).

## ADR-005 File format
Status: Accepted
Context: One file per document, containing everything incl. images visible to others (R-FILE-02), compact ink, future desktop reader (R-FILE-04).
Options: A ZIP container + JSON manifest + protobuf pages + Markdown flows + raw assets; B single SQLite file per document; C one big protobuf; D JSON only.
Decision: A (04-file-format.md). Wire generates Kotlin from `.proto`; the schema doubles as documentation for other readers. Markdown flows are directly readable.
Consequences: whole-file repack on save (mitigated by working copy + STORED assets); schema discipline needed (reserved fields, migrations, golden files).

## ADR-006 PDF export
Status: Accepted (2026-09-28, P01-S5)
Context: Annotated PDF export must keep original PDF pages as vectors; Android's `PdfDocument` cannot import existing pages. PdfBox-Android (last release 2.0.27.0, January 2023) is stale and its BouncyCastle dependency carries known CVEs. Android API level 36.1 added `android.graphics.pdf.component` (stamp annotations with path/image/text objects, `PdfRenderer.write`).
Options: A PdfDocument for Folio pages + PdfBox-Android `LayerUtility` overlay merge for PDF-backed pages (BouncyCastle excluded if possible); B platform stamp annotations (only if the device API level provides them); C raster original page at 200 dpi + vector annotations.
Decision (default): A, behind `PdfExporter` strategies with B and C as fallbacks.
Consequences: one stale third-party library, used only at export time on local files the user created; revisit if a maintained alternative appears.
Evidence 2026-09-28 (P01-S5): Pad 7, `PdfSpikeProbe` run in the debug app (route `spike-pdf`; the separate test APK was refused that day). Source: generated 100-page A4 PDF (PdfDocument: text, rules, one 64 px image per page), 178 KB. Export: 10 overlay pages drawn with PdfDocument (ink curves, label, red mark) merged by `PdfBoxOverlayMerger` (PdfBox-Android 2.0.27.0 `LayerUtility.importPageAsForm` + append content stream), BouncyCastle excluded.
| Measurement | Run 1 / 2 / 3 |
|---|---|
| First page (open + 0.5x preview) ms | 267 / 26 / 25 |
| 512 px center tile per page p50 / p95 ms, zoom 1 | 2.5 / 2.6 (all runs) |
| same, zoom 2 | 2.0 / 2.1 (all runs) |
| Export (overlays + merge + save, 100 pages) ms | 241 / 108 / 80 (overlays 10..11) |
| Output | 202 KB (+13%), 100 pages, all A4, overlay mark red on annotated page, absent on a plain page |
Host test (`PdfBoxOverlayMergerTest`, Robolectric) also shows the merge adds one form XObject only to target pages and works without BouncyCastle. The generated pages are simpler than real scans or papers, so real render times will be higher.
Decision 2026-09-28: A confirmed (merge correct, export 0.24 s vs 10 s budget); BouncyCastle stays excluded (no encrypted PDFs; import of encrypted files is a P08 question).

## ADR-007 LaTeX rendering
Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S4): C jlatexmath-android
Context: Inline and block LaTeX with exact metrics (ascent/depth) so inline math never breaks the grid (R-TXT-04); offline; vector output for PDF export.
Options: A RaTeX (MIT; Rust core with KaTeX-compatible parsing and layout, >99.5% KaTeX syntax coverage claimed, Android binding drawing on Canvas, depth metrics); B zly2006/latex (Kotlin Multiplatform Compose renderer with pre-measure API); C jlatexmath-android (GPL-2 with classpath exception, older); D KaTeX in an offscreen WebView (rejected: slow, async, WebView dependency).
Decision (default): A, via the `MathRenderer` interface so B or C can replace it.
Consequences: native `.so` libraries in the APK (arm64 only is enough for the Pad 7; include arm64-v8a only).
Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S4a, host part): `MathRenderer` + adapters in core:text, corpus testdata/math/corpus.txt (40 formulas), inline style at 50 px (body M at the text reference scale). Host numbers from `MathProbeTest` (Robolectric native graphics); A loads an Android-only `.so`, so its numbers come from `MathProbeInstrumentedTest` on the tablet (P01-S4b). APK delta: clean debug builds with and without the library.
| Option | License | Parsed | Layout+draw p50 / p95 ms | Ink outside box | Vector output | APK delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A RaTeX 0.1.14 | MIT | device (S4b) | device (S4b) | device (S4b) | draws Canvas text, rects and paths only (source); PDF check S4b | +3.54 MB arm64-v8a only (+9.35 MB with 3 ABIs) |
| B huarangmeng latex 1.5.0 (zly2006/latex) | MIT | not built | - | - | no: measuring and export need a Composable scope, export is PNG/SVG only, no Canvas/DrawScope API (README) | - |
| C jlatexmath-android 0.2.0 | GPL-2.0 + linking exception | 39/40 (97.5%, `\ce` unknown) | 0.54 / 1.87 (host) | max 1.85 px, 6 of 39 over 1 px (with `setTrueValues`; the default box adds 0.18 em padding) | Graphics2D over Canvas; PDF check S4b | +0.69 MB |
B fails the vector rule by API, so it was not built. The app now packages arm64-v8a only (also drops about 4.7 MB of other libraries' x86_64/armeabi-v7a natives).
Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S4b, device): `MathProbeInstrumentedTest` on the Pad 7 (passed), 5 warm-up formulas, then 40 formulas x 5 repeats, inline style at 50 px.
| Option | Parsed | Layout+draw p50 / p95 ms | Max ink outside box px (formulas > 1 px) | PDF output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A RaTeX | 40/40 (100%) | 1.49 / 5.09 | 1.56 (4) | vector only (76 KB) |
| C jlatexmath | 39/40 (97.5%, `\ce` unknown) | 0.36 / 0.80 | 1.85 (6) | vector only (49 KB) |
Decision 2026-09-27: C. Rule: success >= 95%, p95 <= 4 ms and vector output; only C meets all three (A misses p95 by 1.1 ms). Both overshoot the box on large operators and accents by up to 2 px at 50 px, so the adapter pads ascent and depth by 0.04 em (A-007). Risks accepted: the library is archived (last release 2020) and GPL-2.0 with linking exception (allowed by .claude/rules/gradle.md with this note); no mhchem `\ce`. A stays the fallback behind `MathRenderer`.

## ADR-008 Text layout engine
Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S3)
Context: Every line must snap to template lines regardless of font (R-TXT-03); long text must stay fast (R-TXT-05); Notewise's slow text-box workflow must not repeat (R-CORE-01).
Options: A Compose text per block with fixed line boxes + per-font baseline correction + cap-height normalization, block-based editing with a single live field; B one BasicTextField per flow (simple, but slow for long text and hard to snap); C fully custom text layout + IME (maximum control, very high cost).
Decision (default): A. Spike fallback: per-line placement from TextLayoutResult metrics if baseline error exceeds 0.5 px.
Consequences: cross-block selection needs custom handling; the focused block shows Markdown markers dimmed (no hidden characters).
Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S3a, host): `BaselineProbeTest` on Robolectric native graphics (host minikin/Skia), 20 bundled fonts x 3 paragraphs (6 to 10 lines), college U = 7.1 mm, body M (cap 0.45 U), text width 175 mm. px = Pad 7 screen px at zoom x fit-width (5.15 px/pt at zoom 1).
| Baseline method | Max baseline error px, zoom 1 / 2 / 4 (all fonts) | Cap-height error px | Layout ms per paragraph (host median) |
|---|---|---|---|
| FONT_DESCENT (ref 4 px/pt, shift = font descent) | 0.64 to 10.35 / 1.28 to 20.7 / 2.56 to 41.4 (fails for all 20) | 0.000 | 0.8 to 4.4 |
| GRID_PITCH (ref round(4U)/U px/pt, shift from first layout baseline) | 0.000 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.7 to 1.2 |
Cause of the drift: `LineHeightStyle` rounds line heights up to whole px and layout baselines are whole px; with 4 px/pt, U = 80.5 px becomes 81 px per line. Golden: core/text/src/test/screenshots/FontSpecimen_compact.png. Device run (`BaselineProbeInstrumentedTest`, tag FolioProbe) is P01-S3b.
Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S3b, device): `BaselineProbeInstrumentedTest` on the Pad 7 (1/1 passed), same fonts and paragraphs: GRID_PITCH 0.000 px at zoom 1, 2 and 4 for all 20 fonts; FONT_DESCENT 0.64 to 10.35 px at zoom 1 (worst: Shadows Into Light, IBM Plex Mono 2.91, Architects Daughter 2.52); cap-height error 0.000 px; layout 0.29 to 0.58 ms per paragraph.
Decision 2026-09-27: A with the GRID_PITCH placement (A-006), a form of the planned TextLayoutResult fallback.

## ADR-009 Index and search
Status: Accepted
Context: Library views, tags, backlinks, full-text search over typed text (R-ORG-03) with files as the source of truth.
Decision: Room database with FTS4, rebuilt from files at any time; manifests carry everything the index needs (no page decoding during scans).
Consequences: index staleness handled by incremental scans and FileObserver; never store user data only in the index.

## ADR-010 Undo model
Status: Accepted
Context: 50 undo steps (R-FILE-05), split view with independent panes, gestures as single steps.
Decision: command pattern with inverses computed at execution; per-pane UndoManager (capacity 50, coalescing window 1000 ms); session-only (not persisted).
Consequences: every mutation must be a command; property tests guard inverse correctness.

## ADR-011 Offline and bundled assets
Status: Accepted
Context: Strictly offline (R-DEV-02) yet Google Fonts, icons, and math fonts are needed.
Decision: no INTERNET permission (removed from merged manifests, verified by `verifyNoInternet`); fonts (OFL), Lucide icons (ISC), and math fonts are bundled; web links open in the user's browser via intents.
Consequences: APK size grows (~15-25 MB); acceptable for a single-device app.

## ADR-012 Build and modules
Status: Accepted
Context: Q51 unanswered; the build is done by an AI agent that benefits from enforced boundaries and fast, focused test runs.
Options: A multi-module with convention plugins (02-modules.md); B single module with packages.
Decision: A. JVM modules for model and format keep most tests fast and Android-free. minSdk = min(35, device SDK) (set in P00-T02); compileSdk/targetSdk = latest stable.
Consequences: more build configuration up front (P00), cheaper and safer changes afterwards.
Note 2026-09-27 (P00-T02): device reports SDK 36 (Android 16, HyperOS OS3.0), so minSdk = 35.
Note 2026-09-27 (P00-T03, A-001): detekt 2.0.0-alpha.6 allowed (build-time only) because compose-rules 0.6.7 requires it and detekt 1.23.8 targets Kotlin 2.0.21; move to stable 2.0.0 when released.

## ADR-013 Navigation
Status: Accepted
Decision: Navigation 3 if a stable release exists at P00-T03, otherwise navigation-compose. Note 2026-09-27 (P00-T03): navigation3 1.2.0 is stable (dl.google.com maven-metadata), so Navigation 3 is used. Few routes (onboarding, library, editor, settings); editor split view is internal state, not navigation.

## ADR-014 Icons
Status: Accepted
Decision: Lucide outlined icons (ISC), converted at build time by `tools:icongen` into Compose ImageVectors. Visually close to the reference's thin outlined style; no icon fonts, no runtime SVG parsing, no material-icons-extended.

# Amendments
Every deviation from docs/architecture or docs/plan is recorded here before or with the change. Newest last.

Format:
## A-NNN YYYY-MM-DD <task-id>: <title>
- Change: what is different from the spec
- Reason: evidence (numbers, errors, API facts)
- Impact: affected docs sections and task ids (updated in the same commit)

## A-001 2026-09-27 P00-T03: detekt 2.0 alpha and hilt-lifecycle-viewmodel-compose
- Change: detekt pinned to 2.0.0-alpha.6 (plugin id `dev.detekt`) instead of a stable release; `androidx.hilt:hilt-lifecycle-viewmodel-compose` replaces `hilt-navigation-compose`.
- Reason: the latest compose-rules (io.nlopez.compose.rules:detekt 0.6.7) depends on dev.detekt:detekt-core 2.0.0-alpha.6 (its POM); the only stable detekt (1.23.8) is built on Kotlin 2.0.21 while the project uses Kotlin 2.4.20 and AGP 9. With Navigation 3 (stable 1.2.0, ADR-013) `hiltViewModel()` lives in hilt-lifecycle-viewmodel-compose; hilt-navigation-compose targets navigation-compose. detekt is build-time only, nothing ships.
- Impact: 02-modules.md#dependencies (DI and Quality rows), decisions.md ADR-012 note, .claude/rules/gradle.md alpha list. Revisit when detekt 2.0.0 is stable.

## A-002 2026-09-27 P00-T04: core:common and core:testing are JVM modules; bytecode 17 without a toolchain
- Change: `core:common` and `core:testing` are Kotlin/JVM modules (spec: Android libraries). `core:testing -> core:model, core:common` is an allowed edge (test-only consumer). No Gradle JVM toolchain: JDK 21 runs the build, bytecode target is 17 via compileOptions / jvmTarget / `--release 17`. build-tools pinned to the installed 37.0.0; compileSdk 37 minor 2.
- Reason: `core:model` and `core:format` are JVM modules and must depend on `core:common` and use `core:testing` in tests; a JVM module cannot depend on an Android library. Both modules only hold pure Kotlin APIs (Android sinks for FolioLog/PerfMonitor tracing live in :app). A toolchain of 17 needs a JDK 17 install or network auto-provisioning; only JDK 21 is installed (env.md). AGP 9.4.1 defaults to build-tools 36.0.0, which is not installed and would trigger a license-bearing download.
- Impact: 02-modules.md#module-list and graph; root `verifyModuleGraph` encodes the graph.

## A-003 2026-09-27 P00-T06: PerfMonitor traces through a TraceSink; Roborazzi plugin via build-logic
- Change: `PerfMonitor` (JVM core:common) emits trace sections through a `TraceSink` interface; :app installs a sink backed by platform `android.os.Trace` instead of androidx.tracing. Release keeps only the trace calls (`PerfMonitor.enabled = BuildConfig.DEBUG`). The Roborazzi Gradle plugin is loaded from build-logic's classpath (Maven Central artifact) instead of the `plugins {}` block.
- Reason: androidx.tracing 2.0.3 reworked its API; the platform Trace (minSdk 35) produces the same Perfetto/atrace sections without an extra dependency and keeps core:common Android-free (A-002). Roborazzi publishes its plugin marker only to the Gradle Plugin Portal, which the build does not use (repositories: google, mavenCentral).
- Impact: 12-performance.md#measurement; tracing-ktx stays in the catalog unused until a module needs it.

## A-004 2026-09-27 P00-REVIEW: qa task layout; test-only EPL-1.0 allowed
- Change: `qa` is layered: each module gets `qa` from `folio.quality`, `verifyNoInternet<Variant>` tasks come from `folio.android.application` (including the androidTest APK manifest), and the root `qa`/`verifyNoInternet` aggregate them (spec: both live in the root build). The gradle rule's license list allows EPL-1.0 for test-only artifacts.
- Reason: per-module tasks keep module builds independent (configuration cache, project isolation later); the root task depends on every module `qa` explicitly (reviewer finding). JUnit4 (EPL-1.0) is required by the testing rule and 02-modules.md#dependencies but never ships in an APK; `verifyModuleGraph` keeps core:testing out of non-test configurations.
- Impact: 02-modules.md#build-logic, .claude/rules/gradle.md.

## A-005 2026-09-27 P01-S1: dry handoff waits for the frame-commit callback
- Change: step 3 of the dry handoff removes finished wet strokes in a `ViewTreeObserver.registerFrameCommitCallback` callback instead of a `Choreographer` frame callback. `DisplayModeHelper` (core:render) exists from P01-S1; P03 wires it into the canvas host.
- Reason: a frame callback posted after `invalidate()` runs in the animation phase of the same vsync, before that frame's draw, so it removes wet ink before the committed layer has drawn it (breaks "never remove earlier"). The commit callback fires after the frame is submitted: `ink:handoff` p50 6.4 ms (about one 120 Hz frame), all post-stroke screenshots clean (decisions.md ADR-002 evidence).
- Impact: 05-canvas-rendering.md#dry-handoff; P03 canvas host tasks (dry handoff, DisplayModeHelper).

## A-006 2026-09-27 P01-S3: grid-pitch reference scale and measured baseline correction
- Change: the line-box layout uses a reference scale r = round(4*U)/U px per pt (one grid unit = whole px) instead of a fixed 4 px per pt, and shifts each block by `k*U*r - firstLineBaseline` from the layout result instead of the font descent from `FontMetricsCache`. Bundled fonts: 37 files (variable where Google publishes them), about 28 MB.
- Reason: Robolectric native-graphics probe, 20 fonts x 3 paragraphs, U = 7.1 mm: the descent shift missed rules by 0.64 to 10.35 px at zoom 1 (2.6 to 41 px at zoom 4) because `LineHeightStyle` rounds each line height up to whole px (80.5 -> 81 px: 0.125 pt drift per line) and layout baselines are whole px. The grid-pitch variant put every baseline on its rule (0.000 px at zoom 1, 2, 4). Confirmed on the Pad 7 (P01-S3b): identical numbers.
- Impact: 07-text-engine.md#line-box, decisions.md ADR-008; P06-T02 (`FontMetricsCache` no longer feeds placement), P06-T03 (`BlockLayout` uses the grid-pitch scale per U).

## A-007 2026-09-27 P01-S4: LaTeX via jlatexmath-android instead of RaTeX
- Change: ADR-007 picks option C (jlatexmath-android 0.2.0) instead of the default A (RaTeX); the RaTeX dependency is removed by P01-T08. `MathBox` gets 0.04 em padding on every side (P01-T08: `\vec` arrows also overshoot sideways).

- Impact: 07-text-engine.md#math, decisions.md ADR-007, docs/notes/env.md; P06-T07 (math adapter, padding, no mhchem support in the corpus tests).

1	# Architecture decisions
2	Compact ADRs. Status values: Proposed (needs spike evidence), Accepted, Superseded. Evidence lines are appended with dates by spikes and reviews (`Evidence YYYY-MM-DD:`). Date of initial decisions: 2026-09-26.
3	
4	## ADR-001 UI stack
5	Status: Accepted
6	Context: Native Android, one tablet, modern animated UI, lowest pen latency.
7	Options: A Kotlin + Jetpack Compose UI with a View-based canvas host; B Compose-only canvas; C Flutter / cross-platform.
8	Decision: A. Compose for all chrome (library, toolbar, sheets, settings). The canvas is a custom `CanvasHostView` embedded with `AndroidView`, with androidx.ink's `InProgressStrokesView` on top.
9	Consequences: pen input bypasses recomposition; Compose remains the productive default elsewhere. Two UI toolkits meet at one well-defined seam (`CanvasController`).
10	
11	## ADR-002 Ink stack
12	Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S1)
13	Context: Wet ink must be as low-latency as possible (R-INK-08); strokes need pressure/tilt brushes, geometry for erasing and lasso, and stable rendering.
14	Options: A androidx.ink 1.1.0-alpha (newest alpha; public brush customization API, fixes since 1.0.0); B androidx.ink 1.0.0 stable (Dec 2025); C custom renderer on androidx.graphics front-buffered surfaces.
15	Decision: A, pinned to an exact alpha. Front-buffered wet ink via `InProgressStrokesView`, finished strokes via `CanvasStrokeRenderer`, geometry for erase/lasso. The experimental mesh-editing partial eraser (1.1.0-alpha05+) is not used because its results are not yet serializable; Folio splits stroke inputs instead (06-ink-input.md#erasers). Our file format stores our own `StrokeInputs`, not ink's serialization, so a library change never breaks files.
16	Fallback: B if an alpha regresses on the device; C only if the spike proves ink unusable on HyperOS.
17	Revisit: when ink 1.1.0 goes stable (move to stable).
18	Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S1): Pad 7, debug build, ink 1.1.0-alpha09, route `spike-ink` (pressure pen, CanvasStrokeRenderer page, DisplayModeHelper), 50 synthetic `input stylus swipe` strokes per run (400 ms, 50 events each). Median of runs, worst in brackets.
19	| Handoff mode | Runs | `ink:onTouch` p50 / p95 / max ms | `ink:handoff` p50 / p95 ms | Janky frames | 3 screenshots after pen-up |
20	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
21	| commit (ViewTreeObserver frame-commit callback) | 3 | 0.20 / 0.28 (0.29) / 0.55 (0.63) | 6.4 / 8.8 (one 66 ms outlier) | 0.8% (1.6%) | stroke shown, all 3 |
22	| frame (Choreographer frame callback) | 1 | 0.20 / 0.28 / 0.49 | 7.8 / 8.2 | 0.4% | stroke shown, all 3 |
23	| immediate (inside `onStrokesFinished`) | 1 | 0.20 / 0.27 / 0.66 | 0.03 / 0.05 | 0.7% | stroke shown, all 3 |
24	Front buffer works on HyperOS: InProgressStrokesView adds a SurfaceView (BLAST, z=1) above the window on the first stroke. Requesting the 144 Hz mode left the display at 120 Hz (device.md#display). Screenshots settle >= 100 ms after pen-up, so single-frame flicker and felt latency are a USER-CHECK. Motion prediction was not wired in the spike (P03).
25	Decision 2026-09-27: A confirmed (p95 0.29 ms vs 1 ms budget, handoff clean). Handoff mode: commit, the only mode that removes wet strokes after the frame showing the committed stroke by construction (A-005).
26	
27	## ADR-003 Committed content rendering
28	Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S2)
29	Context: Dense pages (1500+ strokes, text, images) must pan/zoom at 144 Hz.
30	Options: A software bitmap tiles (512 px) rendered off the main thread; B RenderNode tiles with compositing layers (GPU-cached display lists); C draw all objects every frame.
31	Decision (default): A, because the same code path serves PNG export and it is portable; B if it wins the spike clearly on jank. C rejected (cost grows with content).
32	Consequences: memory budget and tile invalidation logic required; zoom shows scaled tiles briefly until the new bucket renders.
33	Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S2b): Pad 7, route `spike-tiles`, A4 lined page, 1500 seeded strokes (pen/marker/highlighter), 512 px tiles, CanvasStrokeRenderer on a software canvas (A) or RenderNode recording with a compositing layer (B); 3 runs per strategy, median (worst). Display ran at 120 Hz (144 requested). Zoom 1 = bucket 5 (42 tiles incl. ring), zoom 3 = bucket 8.
34	| Metric | A bitmap tiles | B RenderNode tiles |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| zoom-anim 1->3->1 (800 ms each) janky % / p95 / p99 ms | 0.49 (0.50) / 15 (18) / 24 (28) | 0.49 (0.49) / 18 (18) / 22 (24) |
37	| 10 s finger pan at zoom 3, janky % / p95 / p99 ms | 0.06 (0.06) / 9 (9) / 10 (11) | 0.06 (0.06) / 9 (9) / 10 (11) |
38	| tile render p50 / p95 ms, bucket 5 | 3.72 / 8.02 (17.3) | 3.63 / 8.38 (9.29) (recording only; raster happens on the RenderThread) |
39	| tile render p50 / p95 ms, bucket 8 | 2.24 / 4.35 (5.19) | 1.96 / 4.00 (4.22) |
40	| settle (all visible tiles of a new bucket) p50 ms | 97 (106) | 80 (94) |
41	| `tiles:draw` p95 ms | 1.11 (1.39) | 0.82 (1.09) |
42	| meminfo PSS / Graphics / Native heap MiB | 426 / 148 / 202 (Native drops to 125 within seconds) | 272 / 126 / 71 |
43	| pixels differing from a direct software render (zoom 1 / 3) | 0.001% / 0.002% | 1.16% / 0.41% (GPU antialiasing differs) |
44	Both strategies stay far below 1% janky frames and are tied on jank; screenshots show no seams or missing tiles.
45	Decision 2026-09-27: A (tie rule; also pixel-identical to the export raster path). B's lower memory is noted; the tile cache budget (05-canvas-rendering.md#tiles, 25% of largeMemoryClass) must bound A's bitmaps (P03).
46	
47	## ADR-004 Library storage
48	Status: Accepted (2026-09-28, P01-S6)
49	Context: User-visible folder for cross-platform copying (R-FILE-01); fast scanning and random-access ZIP reads; personal sideloaded app.
50	Options: A `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` + `java.io.File` in `Documents/Folio`; B Storage Access Framework tree URI + DocumentFile; C app-specific external storage (`Android/data`), hidden from most file managers.
51	Decision: A. Debug builds use `Documents/Folio-Debug` so tests never touch real notes.
52	Consequences: one-time permission screen; not Play-Store compatible (irrelevant for sideloading). B stays the migration path if a future Android version restricts A.
53	Evidence 2026-09-28 (P01-S6): Pad 7, route `spike-io`, All-files access granted, java.io on `/sdcard/Documents/Folio-Debug` (FUSE). Working copy in app files: 4 x 10 MB random assets (STORED) + 10 x 1 MB pages (DEFLATED) -> 46.0 MB `.folio`.
54	| Measurement | Result |
55	|---|---|
56	| Pack (CRC + ZIP write + fsync + rename + directory fsync), 4 runs | 1391 / 1410 / 1413 / 1450 ms (write 1282..1363, fsync 35..39, rename 13..57, CRC 33..40); directory fsync supported |
57	| Read-back verify (all entries, CRC checked) | ok, 16 entries, mimetype first |
58	| App killed (`stop.sh`) mid-pack, 3 runs | target intact and valid every time; tmp removed by start-up cleanup (1 run) or already gone after the kill (2 runs, FUSE dropped the half-written file) |
59	| FileObserver on `Folio-Debug/fixtures` for `push-fixture.sh` (external writer through FUSE) | CREATE + CLOSE_WRITE (DELETE first when replacing) delivered, under about 150 ms after the push (bound limited by the 6 s `debugcmd.sh` round trip) |
60	| FileObserver during our own pack | CREATE `.tmp`, CLOSE_WRITE, MOVED_FROM `.tmp`, MOVED_TO target |
61	Decision 2026-09-28: A confirmed. Pack stays within 1.5 s for 46 MB with little margin (P11 budget watch: most time is the FUSE write).
62	
63	## ADR-005 File format
64	Status: Accepted
65	Context: One file per document, containing everything incl. images visible to others (R-FILE-02), compact ink, future desktop reader (R-FILE-04).
66	Options: A ZIP container + JSON manifest + protobuf pages + Markdown flows + raw assets; B single SQLite file per document; C one big protobuf; D JSON only.
67	Decision: A (04-file-format.md). Wire generates Kotlin from `.proto`; the schema doubles as documentation for other readers. Markdown flows are directly readable.
68	Consequences: whole-file repack on save (mitigated by working copy + STORED assets); schema discipline needed (reserved fields, migrations, golden files).
69	
70	## ADR-006 PDF export
71	Status: Accepted (2026-09-28, P01-S5)
72	Context: Annotated PDF export must keep original PDF pages as vectors; Android's `PdfDocument` cannot import existing pages. PdfBox-Android (last release 2.0.27.0, January 2023) is stale and its BouncyCastle dependency carries known CVEs. Android API level 36.1 added `android.graphics.pdf.component` (stamp annotations with path/image/text objects, `PdfRenderer.write`).
73	Options: A PdfDocument for Folio pages + PdfBox-Android `LayerUtility` overlay merge for PDF-backed pages (BouncyCastle excluded if possible); B platform stamp annotations (only if the device API level provides them); C raster original page at 200 dpi + vector annotations.
74	Decision (default): A, behind `PdfExporter` strategies with B and C as fallbacks.
75	Consequences: one stale third-party library, used only at export time on local files the user created; revisit if a maintained alternative appears.
76	Evidence 2026-09-28 (P01-S5): Pad 7, `PdfSpikeProbe` run in the debug app (route `spike-pdf`; the separate test APK was refused that day). Source: generated 100-page A4 PDF (PdfDocument: text, rules, one 64 px image per page), 178 KB. Export: 10 overlay pages drawn with PdfDocument (ink curves, label, red mark) merged by `PdfBoxOverlayMerger` (PdfBox-Android 2.0.27.0 `LayerUtility.importPageAsForm` + append content stream), BouncyCastle excluded.
77	| Measurement | Run 1 / 2 / 3 |
78	|---|---|
79	| First page (open + 0.5x preview) ms | 267 / 26 / 25 |
80	| 512 px center tile per page p50 / p95 ms, zoom 1 | 2.5 / 2.6 (all runs) |
81	| same, zoom 2 | 2.0 / 2.1 (all runs) |
82	| Export (overlays + merge + save, 100 pages) ms | 241 / 108 / 80 (overlays 10..11) |
83	| Output | 202 KB (+13%), 100 pages, all A4, overlay mark red on annotated page, absent on a plain page |
84	Host test (`PdfBoxOverlayMergerTest`, Robolectric) also shows the merge adds one form XObject only to target pages and works without BouncyCastle. The generated pages are simpler than real scans or papers, so real render times will be higher.
85	Decision 2026-09-28: A confirmed (merge correct, export 0.24 s vs 10 s budget); BouncyCastle stays excluded (no encrypted PDFs; import of encrypted files is a P08 question).
86	
87	## ADR-007 LaTeX rendering
88	Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S4): C jlatexmath-android
89	Context: Inline and block LaTeX with exact metrics (ascent/depth) so inline math never breaks the grid (R-TXT-04); offline; vector output for PDF export.
90	Options: A RaTeX (MIT; Rust core with KaTeX-compatible parsing and layout, >99.5% KaTeX syntax coverage claimed, Android binding drawing on Canvas, depth metrics); B zly2006/latex (Kotlin Multiplatform Compose renderer with pre-measure API); C jlatexmath-android (GPL-2 with classpath exception, older); D KaTeX in an offscreen WebView (rejected: slow, async, WebView dependency).
91	Decision (default): A, via the `MathRenderer` interface so B or C can replace it.
92	Consequences: native `.so` libraries in the APK (arm64 only is enough for the Pad 7; include arm64-v8a only).
93	Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S4a, host part): `MathRenderer` + adapters in core:text, corpus testdata/math/corpus.txt (40 formulas), inline style at 50 px (body M at the text reference scale). Host numbers from `MathProbeTest` (Robolectric native graphics); A loads an Android-only `.so`, so its numbers come from `MathProbeInstrumentedTest` on the tablet (P01-S4b). APK delta: clean debug builds with and without the library.
94	| Option | License | Parsed | Layout+draw p50 / p95 ms | Ink outside box | Vector output | APK delta |
95	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
96	| A RaTeX 0.1.14 | MIT | device (S4b) | device (S4b) | device (S4b) | draws Canvas text, rects and paths only (source); PDF check S4b | +3.54 MB arm64-v8a only (+9.35 MB with 3 ABIs) |
97	| B huarangmeng latex 1.5.0 (zly2006/latex) | MIT | not built | - | - | no: measuring and export need a Composable scope, export is PNG/SVG only, no Canvas/DrawScope API (README) | - |
98	| C jlatexmath-android 0.2.0 | GPL-2.0 + linking exception | 39/40 (97.5%, `\ce` unknown) | 0.54 / 1.87 (host) | max 1.85 px, 6 of 39 over 1 px (with `setTrueValues`; the default box adds 0.18 em padding) | Graphics2D over Canvas; PDF check S4b | +0.69 MB |
99	B fails the vector rule by API, so it was not built. The app now packages arm64-v8a only (also drops about 4.7 MB of other libraries' x86_64/armeabi-v7a natives).
100	Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S4b, device): `MathProbeInstrumentedTest` on the Pad 7 (passed), 5 warm-up formulas, then 40 formulas x 5 repeats, inline style at 50 px.
101	| Option | Parsed | Layout+draw p50 / p95 ms | Max ink outside box px (formulas > 1 px) | PDF output |
102	|---|---|---|---|---|
103	| A RaTeX | 40/40 (100%) | 1.49 / 5.09 | 1.56 (4) | vector only (76 KB) |
104	| C jlatexmath | 39/40 (97.5%, `\ce` unknown) | 0.36 / 0.80 | 1.85 (6) | vector only (49 KB) |
105	Decision 2026-09-27: C. Rule: success >= 95%, p95 <= 4 ms and vector output; only C meets all three (A misses p95 by 1.1 ms). Both overshoot the box on large operators and accents by up to 2 px at 50 px, so the adapter pads the box by 0.04 em on every side (A-007). Risks accepted: the library is archived (last release 2020) and GPL-2.0 with linking exception (allowed by .claude/rules/gradle.md with this note); no mhchem `\ce`. A stays the fallback behind `MathRenderer`.

107	## ADR-008 Text layout engine
108	Status: Accepted (2026-09-27, P01-S3)
109	Context: Every line must snap to template lines regardless of font (R-TXT-03); long text must stay fast (R-TXT-05); Notewise's slow text-box workflow must not repeat (R-CORE-01).
110	Options: A Compose text per block with fixed line boxes + per-font baseline correction + cap-height normalization, block-based editing with a single live field; B one BasicTextField per flow (simple, but slow for long text and hard to snap); C fully custom text layout + IME (maximum control, very high cost).
111	Decision (default): A. Spike fallback: per-line placement from TextLayoutResult metrics if baseline error exceeds 0.5 px.
112	Consequences: cross-block selection needs custom handling; the focused block shows Markdown markers dimmed (no hidden characters).
113	Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S3a, host): `BaselineProbeTest` on Robolectric native graphics (host minikin/Skia), 20 bundled fonts x 3 paragraphs (6 to 10 lines), college U = 7.1 mm, body M (cap 0.45 U), text width 175 mm. px = Pad 7 screen px at zoom x fit-width (5.15 px/pt at zoom 1).
114	| Baseline method | Max baseline error px, zoom 1 / 2 / 4 (all fonts) | Cap-height error px | Layout ms per paragraph (host median) |
115	|---|---|---|---|
116	| FONT_DESCENT (ref 4 px/pt, shift = font descent) | 0.64 to 10.35 / 1.28 to 20.7 / 2.56 to 41.4 (fails for all 20) | 0.000 | 0.8 to 4.4 |
117	| GRID_PITCH (ref round(4U)/U px/pt, shift from first layout baseline) | 0.000 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.7 to 1.2 |
118	Cause of the drift: `LineHeightStyle` rounds line heights up to whole px and layout baselines are whole px; with 4 px/pt, U = 80.5 px becomes 81 px per line. Golden: core/text/src/test/screenshots/FontSpecimen_compact.png. Device run (`BaselineProbeInstrumentedTest`, tag FolioProbe) is P01-S3b.
119	Evidence 2026-09-27 (P01-S3b, device): `BaselineProbeInstrumentedTest` on the Pad 7 (1/1 passed), same fonts and paragraphs: GRID_PITCH 0.000 px at zoom 1, 2 and 4 for all 20 fonts; FONT_DESCENT 0.64 to 10.35 px at zoom 1 (worst: Shadows Into Light, IBM Plex Mono 2.91, Architects Daughter 2.52); cap-height error 0.000 px; layout 0.29 to 0.58 ms per paragraph.
120	Decision 2026-09-27: A with the GRID_PITCH placement (A-006), a form of the planned TextLayoutResult fallback.

122	## ADR-009 Index and search
123	Status: Accepted
124	Context: Library views, tags, backlinks, full-text search over typed text (R-ORG-03) with files as the source of truth.
125	Decision: Room database with FTS4, rebuilt from files at any time; manifests carry everything the index needs (no page decoding during scans).
126	Consequences: index staleness handled by incremental scans and FileObserver; never store user data only in the index.
127	
128	## ADR-010 Undo model
129	Status: Accepted
130	Context: 50 undo steps (R-FILE-05), split view with independent panes, gestures as single steps.
131	Decision: command pattern with inverses computed at execution; per-pane UndoManager (capacity 50, coalescing window 1000 ms); session-only (not persisted).
132	Consequences: every mutation must be a command; property tests guard inverse correctness.
133	
134	## ADR-011 Offline and bundled assets
135	Status: Accepted
136	Context: Strictly offline (R-DEV-02) yet Google Fonts, icons, and math fonts are needed.
137	Decision: no INTERNET permission (removed from merged manifests, verified by `verifyNoInternet`); fonts (OFL), Lucide icons (ISC), and math fonts are bundled; web links open in the user's browser via intents.
138	Consequences: APK size grows (~15-25 MB); acceptable for a single-device app.
139	
140	## ADR-012 Build and modules
141	Status: Accepted
142	Context: Q51 unanswered; the build is done by an AI agent that benefits from enforced boundaries and fast, focused test runs.
143	Options: A multi-module with convention plugins (02-modules.md); B single module with packages.
144	Decision: A. JVM modules for model and format keep most tests fast and Android-free. minSdk = min(35, device SDK) (set in P00-T02); compileSdk/targetSdk = latest stable.
145	Consequences: more build configuration up front (P00), cheaper and safer changes afterwards.
146	Note 2026-09-27 (P00-T02): device reports SDK 36 (Android 16, HyperOS OS3.0), so minSdk = 35.
147	Note 2026-09-27 (P00-T03, A-001): detekt 2.0.0-alpha.6 allowed (build-time only) because compose-rules 0.6.7 requires it and detekt 1.23.8 targets Kotlin 2.0.21; move to stable 2.0.0 when released.
148	
149	## ADR-013 Navigation
150	Status: Accepted
151	Decision: Navigation 3 if a stable release exists at P00-T03, otherwise navigation-compose. Note 2026-09-27 (P00-T03): navigation3 1.2.0 is stable (dl.google.com maven-metadata), so Navigation 3 is used. Few routes (onboarding, library, editor, settings); editor split view is internal state, not navigation.
152	
153	## ADR-014 Icons
154	Status: Accepted
155	Decision: Lucide outlined icons (ISC), converted at build time by `tools:icongen` into Compose ImageVectors. Visually close to the reference's thin outlined style; no icon fonts, no runtime SVG parsing, no material-icons-extended.

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "**/*.kt"
4	  - "**/*.kts"
5	---
6	# Kotlin rules
7	- Official Kotlin style, enforced by spotless/ktlint. Run `./gradlew spotlessApply` before committing.
8	- Package root `dev.folio`; package mirrors module path (`:core:text` -> `dev.folio.core.text`).
9	- Immutable by default: `val`, data classes, `kotlinx.collections.immutable` for document state.
10	- No `!!` outside tests. No `lateinit` in domain code. Sealed interfaces + exhaustive `when` for variants.
11	- Expected failures return `Outcome<T>` (core:common). Throw only for programmer errors. Never swallow exceptions; log via `FolioLog`.
12	- Coroutines: inject `FolioDispatchers` (main, io, render, pdf, text). No `GlobalScope`, no `runBlocking` on main, cancellation-safe IO.
13	- Hot paths (input, render, text layout, typing) carry a `// HOT PATH` comment: no per-event allocation, no boxing, no logging, no Flow emission per point.
14	- `internal` by default; public only for cross-module API, each with a one-line KDoc.
15	- Units in names when ambiguous: `widthPt`, `sizePx`, `durationMs`, `angleDeg`. Page space = PDF points.
16	- Annotate non-obvious threading with `@MainThread` / `@WorkerThread`.
17	- JSON: kotlinx.serialization. Protobuf: Wire. No Gson, no Java serialization, no reflection-based mappers.
18	- Logging: `FolioLog.d/i/w/e(tag, msg)`. Debug and verbose logs are stripped in release via R8 rules.
19	- Time: inject `Clock` (core:common) instead of `System.currentTimeMillis()` in logic.
20

7	---
8	# Gradle rules
9	- Versions live only in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. Exact pins, no `+`, no ranges, no `latest.release`.
10	- Alpha/beta only where `docs/architecture/decisions.md` allows it (androidx.ink 1.1.0-alpha; detekt 2.0 alpha per A-001).
11	- Convention plugins in `build-logic`: `folio.android.application`, `folio.android.library`, `folio.jvm.library`, `folio.compose`, `folio.hilt`, `folio.room`, `folio.wire`, `folio.screenshot`, `folio.quality`. Module build files stay short (target <= 25 lines).
12	- Adding a dependency: license must be Apache-2.0/MIT/BSD/ISC/OFL (GPL only with classpath exception and an ADR note; EPL-1.0 only for test-only artifacts such as JUnit4, A-004). Check it adds no INTERNET permission. Add a row to `docs/notes/env.md` Dependencies (name, version, license, reason).
13	- Configuration cache and build cache on. `org.gradle.jvmargs` at least `-Xmx4g`.
14	- `verifyNoInternet` stays wired into `qa`. Never remove a check from `qa` to make a task pass.
15	- Never commit `local.properties`, keystores or `keystore.properties`. Release signing reads `keystore.properties` if present, else builds unsigned.
16	- Build types: `debug` (suffix `.debug`), `release` (R8 full mode, shrinkResources), `benchmark` (added in P11, suffix `.benchmark`, debuggable false, signed with debug key).

12	- Flows with Turbine; assertions with Truth.
13	- Golden files in `testdata/` must stay small (< 1 MB each). Large fixtures are generated by test code.
14	- Record screenshot goldens only for intended changes; list them in the commit body ("goldens updated: ...").
15	- Instrumented tests run only via `bash scripts/device/instrumented.sh` against the debug package.
16	- Bug fix = failing test first. Randomized tests use fixed seeds printed on failure.
17	- Flaky test: fix it, or `@Ignore("FLAKY <id>")` + STATUS Deferred entry. Never add retry loops.
18

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "app/**/*.kt"
4	  - "core/**/*.kt"
5	  - "feature/**/*.kt"
6	  - "**/build.gradle.kts"
7	---
8	# Architecture boundaries (violations fail review)
9	Allowed module dependencies:
10	- `core:common` -> nothing internal. JVM module (A-002), no `android.*`.
11	- `core:model` -> core:common. JVM module, no `android.*`.
12	- `core:format` -> core:model, core:common. JVM module, no `android.*`.
13	- `core:storage` -> core:format, core:model, core:common.
14	- `core:ink` -> core:model, core:common.
15	- `core:text` -> core:model, core:common.
16	- `core:render` -> core:model, core:ink, core:text, core:common.
17	- `core:pdf` -> core:render, core:format, core:model, core:common.
18	- `core:designsystem` -> core:common.
19	- `core:testing` -> core:model, core:common. JVM module (A-002), used only via `testImplementation`.
20	- `feature:*` -> any core module. Never another feature.
21	- `app` -> everything. Contains wiring, navigation, Application, debug automation only.
22	
23	Inside features: `ui/` (stateless composables) -> `state/` (ViewModel, UiState, reducers) -> core APIs.
24	- `EditorSession` (feature:editor) owns the document StateFlow, UndoManager, selection, tool state.
25	- The canvas host view talks to the session only through the narrow `CanvasController` interface. It never sees a ViewModel.
26	- Documents change only through `EditCommand`s executed by the session. No direct mutation, no second source of truth.
27	- DI: Hilt, constructor injection, one Hilt module per core library. No service locators, no global singletons outside Hilt.
28	- New module or new cross-module dependency: AMENDMENTS entry + update `docs/architecture/02-modules.md` first.
29

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "core/text/**"
4	  - "feature/editor/**/text/**"
5	---
6	# Text engine rules
7	- Grid invariant: every line box height = k * U (integer k >= 1) and each baseline lies on the rule at the bottom of its line box: baselineY = frame.topPt + sum of line-box heights up to and including that line. Tests assert it for every style.
8	- Font size is derived: size such that cap height = ratio * U (ratio per style) from `FontMetricsCache`. The user picks S/M/L ratios, never raw sp.
9	- Fixed line box via `TextStyle(lineHeight, LineHeightStyle(Alignment.Bottom, Trim.None))` plus per-(font, size) baseline correction. Never rely on font ascent/descent for placement.
10	- Inline math: `MathRenderer` box scaled to fit (ascent <= 0.78 U, depth <= 0.30 U, min scale 0.55). Its placeholder never exceeds the line box.
11	- Headings, block math, tables, rules, code blocks occupy integer line counts.
12	- Blocks are the unit of parsing, layout caching, and editing. Exactly one live text field exists (the focused block).
13	- Parsing: commonmark-java + GFM tables/strikethrough/task lists + Folio inline extensions (`==highlight==`, `$math$`, `[[doc link]]`). Parse per block.
14	- Disable system stylus handwriting on editor fields; a device test asserts the pen draws ink over a focused block.
15	- Budgets: keystroke-to-frame p95 < 16 ms on a 20k-word flow; tap-to-caret < 50 ms. Trace `text:*`.
16

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "core/pdf/**"
4	---
5	# PDF rules
6	- `PdfRenderer` is not thread-safe: one `PdfRasterizer` per document on the single-thread `pdf` dispatcher, one page open at a time, always closed in `finally`.
7	- PDF background tiles are cached apart from content tiles. Annotation edits never re-rasterize the PDF.
8	- Export uses `PdfExporter` with strategies per ADR-006 (PdfDocument for Folio pages, overlay merge for PDF-backed pages, raster fallback). Choose the strategy in one place.
9	- Infinite page export: content bounds + user margin; max 14400 pt per side; split vertically beyond that.
10	- Every export feature has a test that reopens the output with PdfRenderer and checks page count, page size, and pixels at a known annotation.
11	- Imported PDFs are copied into the document assets (sha256 name). Never reference external paths.
12

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "core/ink/**"
4	  - "feature/editor/**/canvas/**"
5	  - "feature/editor/**/input/**"
6	  - "feature/editor/**/tools/**"
7	---
8	# Ink and input rules
9	- Wet ink only through androidx.ink `InProgressStrokesView`. Never render in-progress strokes yourself.
10	- `InputRouter` classifies pointers: stylus/eraser tool types -> active tool; finger -> 1-finger pan, 2-finger pinch zoom; `FLAG_CANCELED` and finger touches within 300 ms of stylus down/hover are dropped (palm). Fingers never draw.
11	- Feed complete MotionEvents (with historical samples) to ink, or StrokeInput batches when a tool modifies input (ruler snapping).
12	- `BrushSpec` <-> `BrushFamily` only via `BrushCatalog` with explicit versions. A visual change = new brush version; old strokes keep theirs.
13	- Dry handoff: `onStrokesFinished` -> `AddObjects` command -> tile update -> after the frame that shows it, `removeFinishedStrokes(ids)`. Never remove earlier.
14	- Persist our `StrokeInputs` (x, y, t, pressure, tilt, orientation). Build `StrokeInputBatch` on load.
15	- Partial eraser splits inputs, not meshes (keeps strokes serializable). One erase gesture = one undo entry.
16	- Tilt, hover, and stylus buttons come from runtime `StylusCapabilities`. Never assume them.
17	- `onTouchEvent` work <= 1 ms p95, zero allocation per event. Trace sections `ink:*` via PerfMonitor.
18

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "core/render/**"
4	  - "feature/editor/**/canvas/**"
5	---
6	# Rendering rules
7	- One renderer: `PageRenderer.draw(canvas, page, regionPt, scale, target)` serves screen tiles, PNG export and PDF export. Targets differ by flags only.
8	- Page space in points. Convert with `Viewport` helpers only.
9	- Tiles: 512 px square, key (pageId, zoomBucket, tx, ty). Background (paper, template, PDF raster) and content tiles are cached separately.
10	- During pan/zoom gestures only transform existing tiles. Re-render at the new bucket after 100 ms idle: visible tiles first, center-out.
11	- Invalidate by bounds via the page spatial index. "Invalidate all" only on page spec/background change.
12	- Tile rendering on the `render` dispatcher (2 threads). Bitmaps come from and return to `BitmapPool`.
13	- Tile cache memory <= 25% of `ActivityManager.largeMemoryClass`. Log evictions in debug builds.
14	- Editor requests the highest refresh-rate display mode while visible (`DisplayModeHelper`) and releases it when hidden.
15	- Renderer changes need Roborazzi goldens. Pan/zoom code changes need a device gfxinfo check.
16

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "feature/**/*.kt"
4	  - "core/designsystem/**"
5	  - "app/src/**/*.kt"
6	---
7	# Compose UI rules
8	- Use design tokens only (`FolioTheme.colors`, `.type`, `.space`, `.shapes`, `.motion`). No raw colors or dp in features except named layout constants.
9	- Stateless composables with hoisted state. `@Preview` light + dark for every screen-level composable.
10	- UiState classes are `@Immutable` and use `ImmutableList`/`ImmutableMap`. Stable keys in lazy lists; `Modifier.animateItem()` for reorders.
11	- Motion only through `FolioMotion` specs (11-design-system.md#motion). Nothing longer than 350 ms.
12	- Touch targets >= 44 dp; icon buttons need content descriptions.
13	- The canvas is an `AndroidView` hosting `CanvasHostView`. Never draw document content or ink with Compose state per frame.
14	- Editor text fields must disable system stylus handwriting (see text-engine rule).
15	- Every new screen state gets a Roborazzi test (landscape + portrait where layout differs).
16	- Layout adapts via window size class; test Pad 7 landscape (expanded) and portrait.
17	- Hardware keyboard: shortcuts go through the editor `ShortcutRegistry`, not ad-hoc `onKeyEvent` handlers.
18

19	/** How a block's baselines are put on grid rules; compared by spike P01-S3 (ADR-008). */
20	enum class BaselineMethod {
21	    /** 07-text-engine.md#line-box as first written: reference scale 4 px/pt, block shifted by the font descent. */
22	    FONT_DESCENT,
23	
24	    /**
25	     * Reference scale chosen so one grid unit is a whole number of px (line pitch exact, no ceil
26	     * drift), block shifted so the first measured baseline lands on its rule.
27	     */
28	    GRID_PITCH,
29	}
30	
31	/**
32	 * One paragraph laid out on the grid: line boxes of one grid unit, baselines on the rule at the
33	 * bottom of each box (07-text-engine.md#line-box). Page positions are points; the block top sits
34	 * on a rule.
35	 */
36	class GridParagraph internal constructor(
37	    private val paragraph: Paragraph,
38	    /** Layout px per pt. */
39	    val refScale: Float,
40	    /** Vertical shift in layout px applied to the paragraph so baselines meet rules. */
41	    val shiftPx: Float,
42	    /** Grid unit U in pt. */
43	    val unitPt: Float,
44	    /** Font size in pt after cap-height normalization. */
45	    val fontSizePt: Float,
46	) {
47	    /** Number of laid out lines. */
48	    val lineCount: Int get() = paragraph.lineCount
49	
50	    /** Height in pt: whole line boxes. */
51	    val heightPt: Float get() = lineCount * unitPt
52	
53	    /** Baseline of [line] in pt below the block top. */
54	    fun baselinePt(line: Int): Float = (paragraph.getLineBaseline(line) + shiftPx) / refScale
55	
56	    /** Draws the block with its top-left at ([leftPt], [topPt]) on a canvas mapping 1 pt to [scale] px. */
57	    fun draw(
58	        canvas: android.graphics.Canvas,
59	        leftPt: Float,
60	        topPt: Float,
61	        scale: Float,
62	        color: Color = Color.Black,
63	    ) {
64	        canvas.save()
65	        canvas.translate(leftPt * scale, topPt * scale)
66	        val k = scale / refScale
67	        canvas.scale(k, k)
68	        canvas.translate(0f, shiftPx)
69	        paragraph.paint(ComposeCanvas(canvas), color = color)
70	        canvas.restore()
71	    }
72	}
73	
74	/**
75	 * Lays out plain paragraphs on a grid with cap-height normalized font sizes
76	 * (07-text-engine.md#line-box, #font-normalization). Spike P01-S3 seed of `BlockLayout`.
77	 */

79	    private val resolver: FontFamily.Resolver,
80	    private val metrics: FontMetricsCache,
81	) {

84	     * placing baselines with [method].

86	    fun layout(
87	        text: String,
88	        family: BundledFontFamily,
89	        unitPt: Float,
90	        capFraction: Float,
91	        widthPt: Float,
92	        method: BaselineMethod,
93	    ): GridParagraph {
94	        val proportions = metrics.proportions(family)
95	        val refScale =
96	            when (method) {
97	                BaselineMethod.FONT_DESCENT -> REFERENCE_SCALE
98	                BaselineMethod.GRID_PITCH -> (unitPt * REFERENCE_SCALE).roundToInt() / unitPt
99	            }
100	        val lineHeightPx = unitPt * refScale
101	        val fontSizePt = capFraction * unitPt / proportions.capRatio
102	        val fontSizePx = fontSizePt * refScale
103	        val style =

109	                textMotion = TextMotion.Animated, // linear, subpixel metrics: line breaks never change with zoom
110	                platformStyle = PlatformTextStyle(includeFontPadding = false),
111	            )

6	import android.graphics.Typeface
7	import androidx.compose.ui.text.font.FontFamily
8	
9	/**
10	 * Em-box proportions of a typeface as fractions of the font size: cap height from the outline of
11	 * "H" (float, unhinted), ascent and descent from the font metrics (positive down, like Paint).
12	 */
13	data class FontProportions(
14	    val capRatio: Float,
15	    val ascentRatio: Float,
16	    val descentRatio: Float,
17	)
18	
19	/**
20	 * Measures and caches [FontProportions] per bundled family (07-text-engine.md#font-normalization).
21	 * Thread-safe; resource fonts load synchronously through [resolver].
22	 */
23	class FontMetricsCache(
24	    private val resolver: FontFamily.Resolver,
25	) {
26	    private val cache = HashMap<String, FontProportions>()
27	
28	    /** Proportions of the regular style of [family]. */
29	    @Synchronized
30	    fun proportions(family: BundledFontFamily): FontProportions = cache.getOrPut(family.name) { measure(typeface(family)) }
31	
32	    /** The platform typeface of the regular style of [family]. */
33	    fun typeface(family: BundledFontFamily): Typeface =
34	        checkNotNull(resolver.resolve(family.fontFamily).value as? Typeface) { "${family.name} did not resolve to a Typeface" }
35	
36	    companion object {
37	        private const val MEASURE_SIZE_PX = 1000f
38	
39	        /** Measures [typeface] at a large size with linear metrics so hinting cannot round the result. */
40	        fun measure(typeface: Typeface): FontProportions {
41	            val paint = measurePaint(typeface, MEASURE_SIZE_PX)
42	            val metrics = paint.fontMetrics
43	            return FontProportions(
44	                capRatio = capHeightPx(paint) / MEASURE_SIZE_PX,
45	                ascentRatio = metrics.ascent / MEASURE_SIZE_PX,
46	                descentRatio = metrics.descent / MEASURE_SIZE_PX,
47	            )
48	        }
49	
50	        /** Height of the "H" outline above the baseline for [paint] (float, from the glyph path). */
51	        fun capHeightPx(paint: Paint): Float {
52	            val path = Path()
53	            paint.getTextPath("H", 0, 1, 0f, 0f, path)
54	            val bounds = RectF()
55	            path.computeBounds(bounds, true)
56	            return -bounds.top
57	        }
58	
59	        /** An unhinted, subpixel-positioned paint like the one text layout uses at the reference scale. */
60	        fun measurePaint(
61	            typeface: Typeface,
62	            sizePx: Float,
63	        ): Paint =
64	            Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG or Paint.LINEAR_TEXT_FLAG or Paint.SUBPIXEL_TEXT_FLAG).apply {
65	                this.typeface = typeface
66	                textSize = sizePx
67	                isLinearText = true
68	            }
69	    }
70	}

5	import androidx.annotation.WorkerThread
6	import dev.folio.core.common.Outcome

8	import org.scilab.forge.jlatexmath.TeXConstants
9	import org.scilab.forge.jlatexmath.TeXFormula
10	import org.scilab.forge.jlatexmath.TeXIcon
11	import ru.noties.jlatexmath.JLatexMathAndroid
12	import ru.noties.jlatexmath.awt.AndroidGraphics2D
13	import ru.noties.jlatexmath.awt.Color
14	
15	/**
16	 * ADR-007 renderer: jlatexmath-android (TeX layout in Java, drawn through a Graphics2D over the
17	 * Canvas, so PDF canvases get vectors). The box uses true TeX metrics plus [PADDING_EM] on every
18	 * side because glyph ink (accents, vector arrows, big operators) exceeds the TeX box by up to about
19	 * 0.04 em (A-007).
20	 */
21	class JLatexMathRenderer(
22	    context: Context,
23	) : MathRenderer {
24	    init {
25	        JLatexMathAndroid.init(context.applicationContext)
26	    }
27	
28	    override val name: String = "jlatexmath"
29	
30	    @WorkerThread
31	    override fun layout(
32	        latex: String,
33	        fontSizePx: Float,
34	        argb: Int,
35	        display: Boolean,
36	    ): Outcome<MathLayout> =
37	        outcomeOf("jlatexmath could not lay out the formula") {
38	            val icon =
39	                TeXFormula(latex)
40	                    .TeXIconBuilder()
41	                    .setStyle(if (display) TeXConstants.STYLE_DISPLAY else TeXConstants.STYLE_TEXT)
42	                    .setSize(fontSizePx)
43	                    .setFGColor(Color(argb))
44	                    .setTrueValues(true) // no 0.18 em insets: the box is the TeX box
45	                    .build()
46	            JLatexLayout(icon, PADDING_EM * fontSizePx)
47	        }
48	
49	    private class JLatexLayout(
50	        private val icon: TeXIcon,
51	        paddingPx: Float,
52	    ) : MathLayout {
53	        private val graphics = AndroidGraphics2D()
54	        private val texAscentPx = icon.trueIconHeight - icon.trueIconDepth
55	        private val padPx = paddingPx
56	        override val box = MathBox(icon.trueIconWidth + 2 * paddingPx, texAscentPx + paddingPx, icon.trueIconDepth + paddingPx)
57	
58	        override fun draw(
59	            canvas: Canvas,
60	            xPx: Float,
61	            baselineYPx: Float,
62	        ) {
63	            // paintIcon puts the TeX box top-left at its origin (no insets); the padding surrounds it.
64	            val save = canvas.save()
65	            canvas.translate(xPx + padPx, baselineYPx - texAscentPx)
66	            graphics.setCanvas(canvas)
67	            icon.paintIcon(null, graphics, 0, 0)
68	            canvas.restoreToCount(save)
69	        }
70	    }
71	
72	    companion object {
73	        /** Extra ascent and depth so drawn ink stays inside [MathBox] (P01-S4: overshoot up to 1.85 px at 50 px). */
74	        const val PADDING_EM = 0.04f
75	    }
76	}

1	package dev.folio.core.common
2	
3	import kotlin.coroutines.cancellation.CancellationException
4	
5	/** Result of an operation that can fail in an expected way (IO, parsing, permissions). */
6	sealed interface Outcome<out T> {
7	    /** The operation produced [value]. */
8	    data class Success<out T>(
9	        val value: T,
10	    ) : Outcome<T>
11	
12	    /** The operation failed; [message] is for logs, [cause] keeps the original exception if any. */
13	    data class Failure(
14	        val message: String,
15	        val cause: Throwable? = null,
16	    ) : Outcome<Nothing>
17	}
18	
19	/** Value on success, null on failure. */
20	fun <T> Outcome<T>.getOrNull(): T? = (this as? Outcome.Success)?.value
21	
22	/** Transforms the success value, keeps failures. */
23	inline fun <T, R> Outcome<T>.map(transform: (T) -> R): Outcome<R> =
24	    when (this) {
25	        is Outcome.Success -> Outcome.Success(transform(value))
26	        is Outcome.Failure -> this
27	    }
28	
29	/** Chains another fallible step. */
30	inline fun <T, R> Outcome<T>.flatMap(transform: (T) -> Outcome<R>): Outcome<R> =
31	    when (this) {
32	        is Outcome.Success -> transform(value)
33	        is Outcome.Failure -> this
34	    }
35	
36	/** Runs [block] and turns exceptions into [Outcome.Failure]. Cancellation is rethrown, never swallowed. */
37	@Suppress("TooGenericExceptionCaught") // Boundary helper: every non-cancellation exception becomes a Failure.
38	inline fun <T> outcomeOf(
39	    failureMessage: String,
40	    block: () -> T,
41	): Outcome<T> =
42	    try {
43	        Outcome.Success(block())
44	    } catch (e: CancellationException) {
45	        throw e
46	    } catch (e: Exception) {
47	        Outcome.Failure(failureMessage, e)
48	    }

14	/**
15	 * ADR-006 option A: draws one-page overlays (annotation layers rendered with PdfDocument) on top
16	 * of pages of an existing PDF as form XObjects, keeping the original page content untouched
17	 * (08-pdf.md#export). Pages without an overlay are copied as they are.
18	 */
19	class PdfBoxOverlayMerger(
20	    context: Context,
21	) {
22	    init {
23	        PDFBoxResourceLoader.init(context.applicationContext)
24	    }
25	
26	    /**
27	     * Writes [output]: [original] with overlay page i of [overlay] appended on top of original
28	     * page [targetPages][i] (0-based). Overlay and target pages must have the same size.
29	     */
30	    @WorkerThread
31	    fun merge(
32	        original: File,
33	        overlay: File,
34	        targetPages: IntArray,
35	        output: File,
36	    ): Outcome<Unit> =
37	        outcomeOf("PDF overlay merge failed") {
38	            PDDocument.load(original, MemoryUsageSetting.setupMixed(MAX_MAIN_MEMORY_BYTES)).use { target ->
39	                PDDocument.load(overlay, MemoryUsageSetting.setupMainMemoryOnly()).use { layers ->
40	                    require(
41	                        layers.numberOfPages == targetPages.size,
42	                    ) { "overlay has ${layers.numberOfPages} pages for ${targetPages.size} targets" }
43	                    val utility = LayerUtility(target)
44	                    targetPages.forEachIndexed { overlayIndex, pageIndex ->
45	                        val form = utility.importPageAsForm(layers, overlayIndex)
46	                        val page = target.getPage(pageIndex)
47	                        // Append mode with a reset context: the original content is wrapped in q/Q first.
48	                        PDPageContentStream(target, page, PDPageContentStream.AppendMode.APPEND, true, true).use { it.drawForm(form) }
49	                    }
50	                    target.save(output)
51	                }
52	            }
53	        }
54	
55	    private companion object {
56	        const val MAX_MAIN_MEMORY_BYTES = 64L * 1024 * 1024
57	    }
58	}

7	data class DisplayModeSpec(

14	/** Id of the fastest mode in [modes] with the resolution of [current], or null if there is none. */
15	fun highestRefreshModeId(
16	    modes: List<DisplayModeSpec>,
17	    current: DisplayModeSpec,
18	): Int? =
19	    modes
20	        .filter { it.widthPx == current.widthPx && it.heightPx == current.heightPx }
21	        .maxByOrNull { it.refreshHz }
22	        ?.id

24	/**
25	 * Requests the highest refresh-rate display mode at the current resolution for [window] while the
26	 * editor is visible, and releases the request when hidden (06-ink-input.md#wet-ink). Main thread only.
27	 */
28	class DisplayModeHelper(
29	    private val window: Window,
30	) {
31	    /** Requests the fastest mode of [display]; returns its refresh rate in Hz, or null if none fits. */
32	    fun request(display: Display): Float? {
33	        val modes = display.supportedModes.map { it.toSpec() }
34	        val id = highestRefreshModeId(modes, display.mode.toSpec()) ?: return null
35	        setPreferredMode(id)
36	        return modes.first { it.id == id }.refreshHz
37	    }
38	
39	    /** Drops the request so the system chooses the mode again. */
40	    fun release() = setPreferredMode(NO_PREFERENCE)
41	
42	    private fun setPreferredMode(modeId: Int) {
43	        val params = window.attributes
44	        if (params.preferredDisplayModeId == modeId) return
45	        params.preferredDisplayModeId = modeId
46	        window.attributes = params
47	    }
48	
49	    private fun Display.Mode.toSpec() = DisplayModeSpec(modeId, physicalWidth, physicalHeight, refreshRate)
50	
51	    private companion object {
52	        const val NO_PREFERENCE = 0
53	    }
54	}

100	                strokeId = wet.startStroke(event, pointerId, brush)
101	            }
102	
103	            MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE -> {
104	                strokeId?.let { wet.addToStroke(event, pointerId, it) }
105	            }
106	
107	            MotionEvent.ACTION_UP -> {
108	                val id = strokeId ?: return true
109	                if (event.flags and MotionEvent.FLAG_CANCELED != 0) wet.cancelStroke(id, event) else wet.finishStroke(event, pointerId, id)
110	                strokeId = null
111	                pointerId = NO_POINTER
112	            }
113	
114	            MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL -> {
115	                strokeId?.let { wet.cancelStroke(it, event) }
116	                strokeId = null
117	                pointerId = NO_POINTER
118	            }
119	        }
120	        return true
121	    }
122	
123	    override fun onStrokesFinished(strokes: Map<InProgressStrokeId, Stroke>) {
124	        val finishedNs = SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos()
125	        committed.strokes.addAll(strokes.values)
126	        committed.invalidate()
127	        pendingWetCount += strokes.size
128	        val remove = {
129	            wet.removeFinishedStrokes(strokes.keys)
130	            pendingWetCount -= strokes.size
131	            PerfMonitor.record(SECTION_HANDOFF, SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos() - finishedNs)
132	        }
133	        when (handoff) {
134	            Handoff.IMMEDIATE -> remove()
135	            Handoff.FRAME -> Choreographer.getInstance().postFrameCallback { remove() }
136	            Handoff.COMMIT -> committed.viewTreeObserver.registerFrameCommitCallback(remove)
137	        }
138	    }
139	
140	    /** The committed-content layer: paper plus every finished stroke, redrawn in full (spike only). */
141	    private class CommittedStrokesView(
142	        context: Context,
143	    ) : View(context) {
144	        val strokes = ArrayList<Stroke>()
145	        private val renderer = CanvasStrokeRenderer.create()
146	        private val identity = Matrix()
147	
148	        override fun onDraw(canvas: Canvas) {
149	            canvas.drawColor(Color.WHITE)
150	            for (stroke in strokes) renderer.draw(canvas, stroke, identity)
151	        }
152	    }
153	
154	    companion object {
155	        const val ROUTE = "spike-ink"
156	        const val SECTION_TOUCH = "ink:onTouch"
157	        const val SECTION_HANDOFF = "ink:handoff"
158	        private const val INK_ARGB = 0xFF1A1A1A.toInt()
159	        private const val BRUSH_SIZE_PX = 6f
160	        private const val BRUSH_EPSILON = 0.1f
161	        private const val NO_POINTER = -1
162	    }
163	}

25	/**
26	 * Spike P01-S3: every bundled font on college-ruled paper (U = 7.1 mm, body M), laid out with the
27	 * selected [BaselineMethod]. Finger drag pans; zoom and method come from `debugcmd.sh spike-fonts`.
28	 * Deleted or promoted by P01-T08.
29	 */
30	@SuppressLint("ViewConstructor") // created in code by AppDebugHooks only
31	@MainThread
32	internal class SpikeFontsView(
33	    context: Context,
34	    private val dispatchers: FolioDispatchers,
35	) : View(context) {
36	    private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + dispatchers.main)
37	    private val resolver = createFontFamilyResolver(context)
38	    private val layouter = GridTextLayouter(resolver, FontMetricsCache(resolver))
39	    private val sidePaddingPx = SIDE_PADDING_DP * resources.displayMetrics.density
40	    private var specimen: FontSpecimen? = null
41	    private var build: Job? = null
42	    private var offsetXPx = 0f
43	    private var offsetYPx = 0f
44	    private var lastX = 0f
45	    private var lastY = 0f
46	
47	    var method = BaselineMethod.GRID_PITCH
48	        private set
49	
50	    /** Zoom as a multiple of fit-width. */
51	    var zoom = 1f
52	        private set
53	
54	    /** Time to lay out all specimen blocks, null while building. */
55	    var layoutMs: Double? = null
56	        private set
57	
58	    /** px per pt at the current zoom. */
59	    val scale: Float get() = (width - 2 * sidePaddingPx) / FontSpecimen.WIDTH_PT * zoom
60	
61	    override fun onAttachedToWindow() {
62	        super.onAttachedToWindow()
63	        rebuild()
64	    }
65	
66	    override fun onDetachedFromWindow() {
67	        scope.cancel()
68	        super.onDetachedFromWindow()
69	    }
70	
71	    /** Lays out the specimen again with [next]. */
72	    fun switchMethod(next: BaselineMethod) {
73	        method = next
74	        rebuild()
75	    }
76	
77	    /** Sets [target] zoom keeping the view center fixed. */
78	    fun applyZoom(target: Float) {
79	        val before = scale
80	        val focusX = width / 2f
81	        val focusY = height / 2f
82	        zoom = target.coerceIn(MIN_ZOOM, MAX_ZOOM)
83	        val k = if (before == 0f) 1f else scale / before
84	        offsetXPx = focusX - (focusX - offsetXPx) * k
85	        offsetYPx = focusY - (focusY - offsetYPx) * k
86	        clamp()
87	        invalidate()
88	    }
89	
90	    override fun onSizeChanged(
91	        w: Int,
92	        h: Int,
93	        oldw: Int,
94	        oldh: Int,
95	    ) = clamp()
96	
97	    override fun onDraw(canvas: Canvas) {
98	        canvas.drawColor(SURROUND_ARGB)
99	        val page = specimen ?: return
100	        canvas.withTranslation(offsetXPx, offsetYPx) { page.draw(this, scale) }
101	    }
102	
103	    @SuppressLint("ClickableViewAccessibility") // spike: drag to pan only, no click action
104	    override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
105	        when (event.actionMasked) {
106	            MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> {
107	                Unit
108	            }
109	
110	            MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE -> {
111	                offsetXPx += event.x - lastX
112	                offsetYPx += event.y - lastY
113	                clamp()
114	                invalidate()
115	            }
116	        }
117	        lastX = event.x
118	        lastY = event.y
119	        return true
120	    }
121	
122	    private fun rebuild() {
123	        build?.cancel()
124	        layoutMs = null
125	        val next = method
126	        build =
127	            scope.launch {
128	                val startNs = SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos()
129	                specimen = withContext(dispatchers.text) { FontSpecimen(layouter, FontRegistry.families, next, compact = false) }
130	                layoutMs = (SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos() - startNs) / NS_PER_MS
131	                clamp()
132	                invalidate()
133	            }
134	    }
135	
136	    /** Centers a page narrower than the view; otherwise keeps at least half a screen of page visible. */
137	    private fun clamp() {
138	        val contentW = FontSpecimen.WIDTH_PT * scale
139	        val contentH = (specimen?.heightPt ?: 0f) * scale
140	        offsetXPx = if (contentW <= width) (width - contentW) / 2f else offsetXPx.coerceIn(width / 2f - contentW, width / 2f)
141	        offsetYPx = offsetYPx.coerceIn(minOf(0f, height / 2f - contentH), height / 2f)
142	    }
143	
144	    companion object {
145	        const val ROUTE = "spike-fonts"
146	        const val MIN_ZOOM = 0.25f
147	        const val MAX_ZOOM = 8f
148	        private const val SIDE_PADDING_DP = 24f
149	        private const val NS_PER_MS = 1_000_000.0
150	        private const val SURROUND_ARGB = 0xFFE9ECF1.toInt()
151	    }
152	}

37	@MainThread
38	internal class SpikeStylusView(
39	    context: Context,
40	    private val dispatchers: FolioDispatchers,
41	) : View(context) {
42	    private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + dispatchers.main)
43	    private val output = File(File(Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory(), BuildConfig.LIBRARY_ROOT), "probe/stylus.json")

46	    private var stats = StylusStats()
47	    private var dirty = true
48	    private var lastX = -1f
49	    private var lastY = -1f
50	    private var lastPressure = 0f
51	    private var lastLine = ""
52	
53	    /** Last write error, or null. */
54	    var writeError: String? = null
55	        private set
56

58	        isFocusable = true
59	        isFocusableInTouchMode = true
60	        setBackgroundColor(BACKGROUND_ARGB)
61	    }
62	
63	    override fun onAttachedToWindow() {
64	        super.onAttachedToWindow()
65	        requestFocus()
66	        scope.launch {
67	            while (isActive) {
68	                if (dirty) write(snapshot())
69	                delay(WRITE_INTERVAL_MS)

72	    }

75	        scope.cancel()

91	            put("writeError", writeError)
92	        }

95	    override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
96	        record(event, hovering = false)
97	        when (event.actionMasked) {
98	            MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL -> stats.onGestureEnd()
99	            MotionEvent.ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS -> stats.onButtonPress(event.actionButton)
100	        }
101	        return true
102	    }
103	
104	    override fun onHoverEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
105	        record(event, hovering = true)
106	        return true
107	    }
108	
109	    override fun onGenericMotionEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
110	        if (event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS) stats.onButtonPress(event.actionButton)
111	        record(
112	            event,
113	            hovering =
114	                event.actionMasked != MotionEvent.ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS && event.actionMasked != MotionEvent.ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE,
115	        )
116	        return true
117	    }

120	    override fun dispatchKeyEvent(event: KeyEvent): Boolean {
121	        if (event.keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK) return super.dispatchKeyEvent(event)
122	        if (event.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN) {

134	        for (line in lines) {

158	            hovering = hovering,

160	            tiltRad = event.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_TILT, pointer),
161	            orientationRad = event.getOrientation(pointer),
162	            distance = event.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_DISTANCE, pointer),
163	            buttonState = event.buttonState,
164	        )
165	        lastX = event.getX(pointer)
166	        lastY = event.getY(pointer)
167	        lastPressure = event.getPressure(pointer)
168	        lastLine =
169	            "${MotionEvent.actionToString(event.actionMasked)} tool=$toolType p=%.3f tilt=%.2f orient=%.2f dist=%.2f buttons=%d hist=%d"
170	                .format(
171	                    lastPressure,
172	                    event.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_TILT, pointer),
173	                    event.getOrientation(pointer),
174	                    event.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_DISTANCE, pointer),
175	                    event.buttonState,
176	                    event.historySize,
177	                )
178	        dirty = true
179	        invalidate()
180	    }

182	    private fun stylusDevices() =
183	        buildJsonArray {
184	            for (id in InputDevice.getDeviceIds()) {
185	                val device = InputDevice.getDevice(id) ?: continue
